subtopics.title: Section A: Objective Items Across Micro and Contemporary Issues

questions.question: Oligopolies that collude in a formal, written manner are called:
Many sellers, differentiated products and easy entry describe:
Prices rising while output falls and unemployment climbs is matched to the term:
Give the term: the point where price equals the minimum of average variable cost, below which production stops. The full-mark answer is:
options: The shutdown point, written out in words

subtopics.title: Short Items: Quick Marks in the Micro Sections

questions.question: Name TWO characteristics of perfect competition. A full-mark pair is:
options: Homogeneous products and free entry and exit

questions.question: Why can a monopolist not charge any price it likes?
options: Because the Competition Commission sets its prices daily
Because the demand curve still rules — at higher prices consumers buy less, so price and quantity are chosen ON the demand curve

questions.question: When a short item says 'name' or 'list', the right response is:
options: A paragraph of explanation for each item
The items alone — explanation spends effort the marks have not paid for

subtopics.title: Data Response: The Monopolist's Graph, Described and Solved

questions.question: On the described graph, the selling price of R150 is read from:
options: The demand curve directly above the equilibrium quantity
The intersection of MC and MR itself
The lowest point of average cost
The vertical axis at zero output

questions.question: Marginal revenue lies below the monopolist's demand curve because:
options: The monopolist has no marginal costs
Selling one more unit requires lowering the price on ALL units, so the last unit adds less than its price

questions.question: With price R150, average cost R125 and output 100 units, total economic profit is:
options: R2 500 — R25 per unit times 100 units

questions.question: If instead average cost were R150 and price R125, the same procedure would show:

subtopics.title: Data Response: Inflation Figures and the Weighted Basket

questions.question: The CPI moves from 120,0 to 127,2. The inflation rate is:
options: 6,0 percent — 7,2 divided by the OLD index of 120,0, times 100

questions.question: Food weighted 40% up 8%, transport 35% up 6%, education 25% up 4%. The weighted increase is:
Low-income households often experience worse-than-headline inflation because:
options: Their real baskets are food-heavy, so food price surges hit them at greater weight

questions.question: If fuel and electricity led the increases, the inflation is best classified as:
options: Demand-pull, cured by the repo rate alone
Cost-push — and the repo rate cools spending without cheapening fuel

subtopics.title: The Eight-Mark Paragraphs: Graphs in Words and Judgements in Context

questions.question: In the kinked demand curve, a lone price INCREASE loses many customers because:
options: Demand above the kink is elastic — rivals hold their prices and shoppers switch
Demand above the kink is inelastic

questions.question: The kink pushes oligopolists toward:
options: Non-price competition — advertising, branding and service — because price moves lose revenue both ways

questions.question: A balanced minimum wage evaluation concludes that:
options: All workers lose from wage floors
The outcome depends on the level set and enforcement — a modest floor helps more than it harms; an aggressive one costs jobs
Employers set wages fairly without any floor

questions.question: Tradeable pollution permits control river pollution by:
options: Capping total discharge and letting firms trade the right to pollute within the cap

subtopics.title: The Essay, Built Live: Compare and Contrast Market Structures

questions.question: The essay's forty marks divide as:
options: Introduction 2, main body 26, additional part 10, conclusion 2

questions.question: In the comparison body, each developed contrast — such as horizontal against downward-sloping demand — earns:
options: Two marks when fully explained in context
Marks only if a diagram is drawn

questions.question: The monopoly's long-run economic profit, described verbally, is:
options: The area under the marginal cost curve
The rectangle between price and average cost across the equilibrium quantity, persisting because barriers block entry

questions.question: A strong additional part on monopoly argues that:
options: Monopolies are always evil in every case
Monopolies never exist in South Africa
Economies of scale can justify regulated natural monopolies, while unregulated dominance harms consumers — hence the Competition Act

subtopics.title: The Second Essay Option: Combating Inflation, Planned to the Mark

questions.question: The measure that attacks DEMAND-PULL inflation most directly is:
options: Raising the repo rate to make credit dearer and cool spending

questions.question: Discipline over administered prices such as electricity tariffs fights inflation on:
options: The cost-push side — it removes a supply-side price engine directly

questions.question: A fair evaluation of South African inflation targeting credits it with:
options: Anchoring expectations and predictability since 2000, while noting its weakness against cost-push shocks

questions.question: The conclusion 'the cure must match the cause' earns its two marks because it is:
options: A summary of every body fact
A fresh closing judgement the body supports but has not already stated
